tables.name: table_01.csv
tables.caption: Table 1: Results on the test sets. We report the mean score over 5 runs. Standard deviations in score are around 0.1 for NER, FGN, and translation, 0.02 for POS, and 0.05 for the other tasks. See the appendix for results with them included. The +Large model has four times as many hidden units as the others, making it similar in size to the models when ELMo is included. * denotes semi-supervised and † denotes multi-task.

tables.name: table_02.csv
tables.caption: Table 2: Dev set performance of multi-task CVT with and without producing all-tasks-labeled examples.

tables.name: table_03.csv
tables.caption: Table 3: Ablation study on auxiliary prediction modules for sequence tagging.

tables.name: table_04.csv
tables.caption: Table 4: Comparison of single-task models on the dev sets. “CVT-MT frozen” means we pretrain a CVT + multi-task model on five tasks, and then train only the prediction module for the sixth. “ELMo frozen” means we train prediction modules (but no LSTMs) on top of ELMo embeddings.

tables.name: table_05.csv
tables.caption: Table 5: Results on the test sets for all tasks. We report the means and standard deviations of 5 runs. The +Larger model has four times as many hidden units as the others, making it similar in size to the models when ELMo is included. For dependency parsing, we omit results from Choe and Charniak (2016), Kuncoro et al. (2017), and Liu and Zhang (2017) because these train constituency parsers and convert the system outputs to dependency parses. They produce higher scores, but have access to more information during training and do not apply to datasets without constituency annotations. * denotes semi-supervised and † denotes multi-task.

tables.name: table_07.csv
tables.caption: Table 7: Error rates on semi-supervised CIFAR-10. We report means and standard deviations from 5 runs. CIFAR-10+ refers to results where data augmentation (random translations of the input image) was applied. For some of our models we add a random or adversarially chosen perturbation to the student model’s inputs, which is done in most consistency regularization methods.
